sentences.text: This second bail application under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 438 of Cr.P.C.) has been filed by the applicant- Deepak S/o Late Shri Manohar Ji Katakwar for grant of anticipatory bail, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.71/2022 registered at Police Station Neelganga, District Ujjain (M.P.) for commission of offences under Sections 420 and 409 of IPC.

His first application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 26.07.2023 in M.Cr.C.No.60617/2022.
2.

As per prosecution story, applicant Deepak, General Manager of M.P. State Development Corporation submitted an application mentioning that M/s.Topworth Tollways Ujjain Pvt. Ltd. was assigned maintenance and operation work of Ujjain-Jaora road under BOT scheme and the company started collecting toll since 2013.

The collection was to be deposited in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6637 2 MCRC-44026-2024 Escrow Account of the State Bank of India and the money was to be withdrawn as per terms and conditions agreed upon, but in violation of the terms and conditions, the bank account was declared NPA and after that without permission an account in District Co-operative Central Bank, Ujjain was got opened and the collected amount was started to be deposited in that account.

The fund was diverted without any permission for taking undue benefit which comes under the economic offence, therefore, FIR vide Crime No.71/2022 was registered at Police Station Neelganga, district Ujjain.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has not committed any offence.

National Company Law Tribunal in the year 2020 declared M/s.Topworth Tollways Ujjain Pvt. Ltd.
as bankrupt and after that for operation purpose vide resolution, professionals were appointed.
It is undisputed that the amount collected was to be deposited in Escrow account.

sentences.text: operation purpose and for this, applications were also filed for permission, but when permission was not granted, an account in District Cooperative Central Bank was opened and an amount of Rs.23 Crores were deposited.
No amount has been misappropriated.
The account in the District Co-operative Central Bank was opened only to pay to vendor companies and salary to the Directors.
National Company Law Tribunal has found that no offence has been committed by the applicant.
There is no sufficient evidence available on record to establish the complicity of the accused with the alleged crime.
There is no likelihood of his absconding or tampering with evidence.
He will cooperate with the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:6637 3 MCRC-44026-2024 investigation.
On these contentions, learned counsel prays for allowing the application for grant of anticipatory bail.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has vehemently opposed the prayer on the ground that admittedly an account in District Co-operative Central Bank was opened in defiance of the terms and conditions for siphoning of the funds collected from the Toll, investigation is going on therefore, prays for dismissal of the anticipatory bail application.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

In the aforesaid factual backdrop, when prima facie it is clear that funds have been diverted and not deposited in the Escrow account as agreed upon, investigation is going on, looking to the amount involved in this case and evidence collected in its entirety, this Court is not inclined to grant benefit of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, this second anticipatory bail application filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is dismissed.
